the fused-GDN-MTP kernel gap is NOT sidestepped by switching drafter. Read in the Thor's OWN running container (vllm 0.26.1rc1.dev942+g5a4c8d992), model_executor/layers/mamba/gdn/qwen_gdn_linear_attn.py:1798 _can_use_fused_gdn_mtp_decode gates on 'spec_sequence_masks is not None and num_decodes == 0 and num_spec_decodes > 0' — a property of the TARGET's verification batch, not of which drafter produced it. DSpark's block-7 verification is a spec-decode batch, and its width 8 is <= MAX_FUSED_GDN_MTP_TOKENS (8), so DSpark would launch the same fused_gdn_decode_post_conv_mtp kernel that killed the d1 first decode

VLLM_GDN_DECODE_KERNEL=triton is the unlock, and it is a first-class vLLM env var (envs.py:131 and :1211, Literal['cuda','triton'], default 'cuda'). qwen_gdn_linear_attn.py:491-505 reads it, and :1807 makes 'gdn_decode_kernel == cuda' a REQUIRED conjunct of the fused-MTP gate — so setting triton routes the target's GDN layers down _forward_core (the Triton spec path) and the missing-image kernel is never launched. This turns the d1 'MTP MUST BE OFF on sm_110' blocker from a hard wall into a config knob, and it applies to MTP-n2 and DSpark alike

claims.text: vLLM's own auto-fallback cannot detect this failure: _fused_gdn_decode_unsupported_reason (qwen_gdn_linear_attn.py:511-533) tests gqa layout, head dims, dtypes, has_device_capability(80), and hasattr(torch.ops._C,'fused_gdn_decode_post_conv_mtp'). On sm_110 the symbol IS built and capability IS >= 8.0 — the wheel just ships no sm_110 SASS image for it — so every guard passes and the failure surfaces at kernel launch. That is why d1 saw a crash on first decode instead of a graceful Triton fallback, and it matches the cuda-wheel-arch lesson (Spark sm_121 vs Thor sm_110 are not one arch)

claims.text: the 1M YaRN window and DSpark cannot both survive on the Thor. The Spark refused the DSpark boot at max_model_len=1048576 / util 0.58 ('needs 51.47 GiB KV; available 40.76'), and the Thor is strictly worse per GiB of KV: it runs kv_cache_dtype=auto (the validated #109 divergence) where the Spark runs fp8, and its 1M pool is 1,114,504 tokens vs the Spark's 1,271,476 at the same util. So any Thor speculation arm inherits the same forced trade-down to the checkpoint's native 262144 — a served-contract change visible through lobes capabilities, not a private dial

claims.text: do not chase the published 34-38 tok/s DGX Spark figure on the Thor. It is PUBLISHED-ELSEWHERE — a different publisher's checkpoint (RadixArk NVFP4), a different engine (SGLang), a different target quantization, on different silicon (sm_121, not sm_110). docs/dspark-speculation.md already records that this fleet measured its own numbers rather than closing that gap, and a Thor run widens the gap rather than narrowing it

a single-shape throughput number is not a description of a speculative lane. The Spark spike measured a ~3x content spread (DSpark 46.20 code / 31.73 reasoning / 13.71 prose tok/s at 262144) and recorded ~10-13% single-run variance, so any Thor arm must run at least the same three content shapes, label every number with the shape that produced it, and treat deltas at or under ~15% as noise

MTP-n2 and DSpark have IDENTICAL sm_110 exposure — a hypothesis I formed and then REFUTED by reading the source, recorded so it is not re-argued. I expected the checkpoint's own MTP head to run GDN layers (making MTP the riskier arm on sm_110) and DSpark's separate dense drafter to be cleaner. It is not so: qwen3_5_mtp.py:118-124 builds the MTP head's decoder layers with layer_type='full_attention', and qwen3_dspark.py's drafter is likewise full-attention GQA. NEITHER drafter touches GDN. The only fused_gdn_decode_post_conv_mtp exposure is the TARGET's verification batch, which VLLM_GDN_DECODE_KERNEL=triton covers identically for both. Drafter choice is therefore a pure throughput question on this box, not a kernel-risk question

no quality claim rides on this, and an observed divergence triggers INVESTIGATION before any verdict. Block speculation is lossless BY CONSTRUCTION (the target verifies every drafted token) — docs/dspark-speculation.md labels that STRUCTURAL, not measured, and explicitly notes it is 'not a claim that any particular implementation is bug-free: a broken verification path, a mangled config, or a silently-disabled speculative flag can all violate it in practice'. A Triton-vs-CUDA GDN decode swap is a further axis again, touching the non-speculative path too. So this spike measures speed and acceptance only; if an output difference IS observed on a speculative arm, the correct first move is to determine whether it is an implementation defect (config, verification path, parser) or a genuine algorithmic divergence — the structural claim is about the algorithm, and a defect falsifies the deployment, not the algorithm

open_vagueness.resolution: resolved by design, not by measurement: the spike's FIRST arm is a triton + no-speculation control, run same-day on the same harness (claim c14). That makes the Triton path's cost on the unspeculated decode a MEASURED OUTPUT of this work rather than an unknown blocking it. If the control comes in materially below the 2026-08-20 cuda-path 12.1 tok/s, that is itself a reportable finding and may end the spike with 'keep the cuda path, no speculation' — a valid outcome under c16

open_vagueness.text: whether the thor card should stop borrowing spark-lobe. lobes/profiles/schema.py:136 SPECULATIVE_CONFIG_ROLES now includes cortex, so builtin/thor.toml COULD finally declare speculative_config='' and encode the sm_110 MTP-off fact that today lives only as a prose comment (thor.toml:35-39) plus a hand-edit on the box. But a shape override composes ON TOP of the card, so spark-lobe's DSpark value would beat it — the exact precedence gap issue #204 tracks. The alternative is a thor-cortex shape, for which orin-cortex.toml is the existing precedent

whether choosing 262144 should ALSO retire the YaRN hf_overrides block. The operator's stated reason for 262144 is model quality at the native ceiling, which argues for stock rope too — but spark-lobe.toml keeps hf_overrides deliberately because every DSpark arm was measured with it in force, and the 2026-08-19 QA pass found zero quality cost from always-on YaRN (7/8 native vs 7/8 YaRN, identical failure — 8 prompts, thin). Retiring it needs its own transcript at 262144 + stock rope; do not fold it into the speculation spike as a second uncontrolled variable
